newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold ends up on silver, shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends up on silver, shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended higher on Friday compared to New York's previous close on the back of silver buying and shortcovering after a day of choppy trading, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$352.50/353.00 an ounce against New York's $351.25/75 close on Thursday.
"Silver is the one being bought and helping gold up," said a senior precious metals trader at an international bank.
Other traders added that silver could well skyrocket if it was not bogged down by gold.
"There is a huge ratio between buying silver and selling gold and that's fuelling the run-up too," a bullion dealer said.
Dealers reported large call options being bought at $5.00 on silver and noted the market was being largely driven by silver at the moment.
Gold rose following shortcovering, dealers said, adding that if gold fell slightly, more shortcovering could follow.
"A lot of people are still short $350 put, and if we go back down we'll see more of a choppy market as people have to shortcover in the spot market," said an options trader.

Physical gold premiums were still high -- between 120 and 160 U.S. cents over the loco London market -- and dealers said players were reluctant to bring in gold bars as demand would snuff out during the Chinese New Year holiday in February.
Local gold ended HK$28 higher at HK$3,254 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous fix at -6.00.
